newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bancaire sells units to Bank of New York.
newsitem.headline: Bancaire sells units to Bank of New York.

text.p: French finance house Compagnie Bancaire said on Tuesday it has agreed to sell British units UCB Invoice Discounting Ltd and UCB Factoring Ltd to Bank of New York Financial Corp.

The two companies being sold "form one of the largest UK independent receivable finance groups (not owned by a UK clearing bank) with combined advances outstanding of 171 million stg and net assets of 8.8 million stg at 30 November 1996," Cie Bancaire said in a statement.
The companies hold six percent of the market, a Cie Bancaire spokeswoman said. She declined to give the value of the deal.
The sales are a further step in restructuring UCB's British subsidiary UCB Group Plc, which sold UCB Home Loans Corporation to Nationwide Building Society in 1995.

Cie Bancaire is considering various options in the British commercial mortgage market, including the sale of part of its assets and operations, following an internal review of its strategic position, Cie Bancaire said. It expects to make a statement before the end of 1997.
The restructuring of UCB Group Plc is not expected to have significant net impact on Cie Bancaire's 1997 results, it said.
Cie Bancaire will develop UFB Humberclyde, a British subsidiary specialising in business equipment finance, with a short-term finance division which will not compete with the companies being sold.
Baring Brothers International Ltd advised Cie Bancaire on the transaction.
